title: You're Paying 19% More AND Wasting 30%
editorialNotes: 19.1% (BLS CPI, April 2026) and 30% waste are sourced per the Notion index; kept as headline text, not hero type. The $3,900 and $1,950 figures are derived by the script from $250/week and are body copy only.
Eggs +64% is sourced to 2024 BLS data (stale); beef +22% and vegetables +18% have no index entry.

thread.element: grocery receipt total ticking up with a trash can filling beside it

copy.headline: Grocery prices are up 19.1% since 2022. You're also wasting 30% of what you buy.
If you spend $250/week on groceries (national average for a household of 4), that's $13,000/year.
Inflation made the waste problem worse, not better.
copy.body: Every wasted item costs more than it did 4 years ago. You're not just losing food. You're losing inflated food.

copy.headline: The biggest inflation categories are also the most wasted:
items: These are the exact items people overbuy and forget.

copy.headline: Cutting waste by 50% at today's prices saves the average household roughly $1,950/year.
copy.body: That's a vacation. That's 3 months of car payments. That's real money — not a coupon.
